messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 detected: elevated latency + 5xx for route /v1/generate (model: rdx-13b-opt) — automatic alert triggered at 2026-03-15T14:07:24Z
maria: seeing p95 token generation latency jump 120ms -> ~1.2s across the fleet serving that route. Errors up ~6x. KV cache evictions spiked 30x in last 10m.
maria: continuous-batching queue length growing, cont-batch backlog ~450 reqs pending on a subset of allocs.
kevin: suspect recent rollback of default batching limits in the config-> CI change earlier today? There was a PR that bumped max_num_seqs default to 64.
kevin: if max_num_seqs is too high we assemble huge batches and then the KV cache paging thrashes when sequence footprints vary — leads to inflated memory and timeouts.
dinesh: I can roll a quick mitigation: either reduce max_num_seqs and max_batch_tokens or flip continuous_batching=false for the route. Which is faster?
maria: flipping continuous_batching off for that route is fastest (no model restart). It forces single-request paths and avoids the batching assembly. Do it on the node pool serving zephyr-prod first.
kevin: alternative short fix: set max_batch_tokens=1024 and max_num_seqs=8 and increase assemble_timeout_ms to 300. That reduces batch size and gives KV more predictable caching.
liz: customer Zephyr on that route has a crop of high-frequency small requests; their UX is seeing ~5x latency and occasional 504s. We should call them after mitigation.
sre-oncall: tagging followup runbook items. I'll hand off monitoring to liz after mitigation.
dinesh: Applying quick config change via internal CLI now.
--- command ---
$ redwood-cli config set-route zephyr-prod --patch '{"continuous_batching": false}'
Applied to 3 allocs: alloc-22, alloc-23, alloc-24
--- output ---
ok: route config patched (no restart).
maria: rolling the change now across the region, watching latency panels.
kevin: good — also please snapshot /proc/mem and KV eviction logs before next change.
maria: copying logs:```
2026-03-15T14:08:01Z runtime: cont_batch assemble for route /v1/generate: candidate_count=56 total_tokens=73240
2026-03-15T14:08:02Z runtime: kvcache: page_eviction rate=312/s (baseline 8/s)
2026-03-15T14:08:02Z runtime: OOM-guard triggered on alloc-23 while assembling batch -> partial failure
2026-03-15T14:08:03Z proxy: upstream 504 from alloc-23
```
kevin: those numbers match the hypothesis. Cont-batch built super-large batches (total_tokens 73k) and then the runtime paged heavily.
dinesh: continuous_batching=false applied, initial allocs show immediate drop in cont-batch queue to 0 and p95 latency falling back under 200ms on patched allocs.
maria: good — overall p95 across the region now ~210ms down from 1.2s. Errors trending down.
liz: sending note to Zephyr support that we're mitigating and will confirm stable in 15m.
kevin: follow-up hotfix we should apply to config defaults: set max_num_seqs=8, max_batch_tokens=2048, assemble_timeout_ms=300 for any route with small-request traffic patterns. Also add a per-route override for high-throughput streaming routes.
sre-oncall: creating an alert: KV cache churn ratio > 10x baseline + cont-batch backlog > 200 -> page engineering pager.
dinesh: pushing a more surgical change for safety:```
$ redwood-cli config set-route zephyr-prod --patch '{"continuous_batching": true, "max_num_seqs": 8, "max_batch_tokens": 2048, "assemble_timeout_ms": 300}'
Applying to 3 allocs... ok
```
maria: after the surgical change, latency stable and no further evictions. Monitor for 30m before we close.
liz: updating customer: "We're seeing requests return to normal; a config change temporarily disabled aggregation then applied safer limits. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."
kevin: note for postmortem: root cause = PR that increased global default max_num_seqs without a traffic-pattern gating. Secondary cause = missing alert for KV cache churn + cont-batch queue length.
sre-oncall: handoff: I'll be taking the summary + timeline. @liz you own customer comms and verification. @kevin + @dinesh add config change PRs and regression tests.
maria: monitoring shows stable for 18m, p95 < 250ms, errors baseline.
liz: will keep on-call in copy and escalate if any regressions.
kevin: immediate action items: 1) revert risky default in our infra repo 2) add unit/integration test that simulates small-variable sequences and ensures max_batch_tokens cap enforced 3) add KV-churn alert.
dinesh: I'll open a hotfix PR with the safer defaults and include a migration note.
sre-oncall: logging this as SEV2 -> recovery. Creating incident record and assigning postmortem owners.
maria: thumbs up :thumbsup: — great rapid triage.
liz: final note before close: impacts: ~3 enterprise customers saw transient latency and some 504s for ~12–18 minutes; no data loss. We have committed timeline and immediate mitigations.
incident-bot: Incident status changed to RECOVERED at 2026-03-15T14:35:17Z
